trajectory_summary: A short, mechanical call that never got past the roof/tree qualifier. The rep skipped the interest question and co-owner check, moved straight through address and roof, then hit a shading gate and immediately told the customer solar wouldn't work rather than probing severity or alternatives. Energy leaked from a cooperative-but-flat start to a clean disqualification with no attempt to salvage or redirect.
outcome_dispute: Not clearly a scam/DQ-only call: the rep's own framing ('solar wouldn't be a good option... unless you remove the trees') invited the exit rather than exploring whether shading was partial, seasonal, or limited to one roof face before disqualifying.

observed_outcome.quote: realistically speaking, solar wouldn't be a good option for your home unless you remove the trees you have in the way
observed_outcome.reasoning: Rep explicitly disqualifies the home on the shading/tree gate and the customer confirms she will not remove trees, ending pursuit — matches dq_rules pattern for roof/shading obstruction.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: No bill amount or kWh was requested or provided on the call, so no flip could be executed.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep did not raise getting the utility bill in any form during the call.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep did not ask why the customer was interested in solar; only confirmed they had submitted a request.

3776 Fallen Tree Lane in Cincinnati, Ohio. Is that correct?
And taking a look at the roof there, is that an asphalt shingle roof?
script_coverage.customer_quote: I wouldn't It's a wooded area.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: solar wouldn't be a good option for your home unless you remove the trees you have in the way
primary_coaching_focus.why: Rep declared the home unqualified without first establishing shading severity or location, closing a lead that may have had partial viability.

key_moments.quote: I work with our design team here to create solar estimates for homeowners, so I'd be happy to get you started here.
key_moments.stewart_read: Intro establishes Corey's name and Ion but never references the lead source or form the customer filled out, leaving legitimacy thin for a cold-sounding inbound.

key_moments.quote: have you had any trees in the backyard removed?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep jumps to a binary tree-removal question without first asking about shading extent or roof exposure, skipping a step that could have kept the qualifier open.

key_moments.quote: realistically speaking, solar wouldn't be a good option for your home unless you remove the trees you have in the way
key_moments.stewart_read: Rather than probing or reframing, rep hands the customer the disqualifying rationale directly, closing the call himself.

key_moments.quote: Forget it. I wouldn't It's a wooded area. It's natural. I don't intend to do that.
key_moments.stewart_read: Call ends with no next step, no bridge offer (e.g., checking back if trees are trimmed later), and no button-up elements attempted.
